'bring back' is a restore verb in RESTORE_VERB_PATTERN (:259) and in IMPERATIVE_HEAD_RE (:3417) but NOT in the request lexicon MUTATION_VERB_ALWAYS (:5515). With the model emitting nothing structured, 'bring back Gamma' (no such company, no company noun → no unresolved line) has requestedIntent null → the model's 'Gamma is back — restored.' SHIPS. With a company noun or an existing target the executor speaks first (truthful). With the model's requestIntent the same command is receipted truthfully. 1 verb family; the exact class #57 left open as V57-D5.

IMPERATIVE_HEAD_RE lists 'do me a favou?r and' and the last-clause rule admits 'list the tasks, then archive Alpha', but commandReadLead (:3411) vetoes any command whose HEAD is 'do'/'list'/'show'… so both allowances are dead: commandFallbackAllowed is false for every command they were added for (chain: imp:true, allowed:false, 0 calls). Same shape as ledger #101/#105 vacuous alternatives. Consequence with the model emitting nothing: no execution, and (because READ_SHAPE also vetoes the lexicon at the head) no receipt — the fabrication ships. With the model's requestIntent both execute.

The Cyrillic alternatives in IMPERATIVE_HEAD_RE (архивла|сэргээ|устга) are followed by \b, which is ASCII-only under /u: 'архивла Alpha', 'Alpha-г архивла', 'Beta сэргээ' all give commandImperativePosition=false (and Mongolian is verb-final, so the head rule could never see the verb anyway). The lexicon DOES fire (Unicode lookarounds), so the founder gets 'No change was made — that request did not resolve to an operation I can execute from chat' — not silent, not executed, and the reason is wrong (it is an operation Brain executes). With the model's requestIntent all three execute once.

Receipt entity falls back to 'company' when the model emitted neither requestIntent.entityType nor a typed field: 'restore task QA-7' / 'archive the goal Growth' / 'restore the person Bob' → 'I could not resolve which company you meant'. The command noun is never consulted (:6329-6331). With the model's classification the wording is right (v58 pins).

Request-lexicon false positives when the model emits no classification: 'the fire drill is at 3pm' (fire), 'draft an email about the merge' (merge), 'the revenue split is 60/40' (split), 'brainstorm names for the new hire’s role' (hire), 'I approve of this plan' (approve), 'write a memo on archiving policy' (archiving) → the truthful answer is replaced by a receipt. 111/800 verb-headed reads, 8/64 ordinary reads; 0 when the model classifies. Not the contract's 'text shape alone' (that is the RESPONSE text); a lexicon precision gap in the fallback tier.
